findings.found: Bank-letter dates printed as 10/07/2026 or 9 November 2026 were not matched to the ISO date the reader returns, so the 90-day check silently skipped them.
findings.fix: Dates are compared as dates (all common styles); a bank letter without a verifiable date now asks the vendor (DOC_UNDATED).

findings.found: A fraudster pasting over only the account NUMBER (not the whole 'IBAN: ...' line) was not detected.
findings.fix: Two different texts drawn at the same spot of a page are flagged as a pasted-over value, whatever the field.

findings.found: The account holder was never screened: a clean company asking to be paid into a sanctioned party's account was not rejected.
findings.fix: Form and bank-letter account holders are screened against the sanctions list.

findings.found: A name containing a sanctioned entity's whole distinctive name ('Meridian Crest Logistics') was approved.
findings.fix: Sharing the full distinctive part of a listed name goes to compliance review.

findings.found: Payments to a third party (factoring company, a director personally) were sent back to the vendor instead of a reviewer.
findings.fix: Policy change: a clearly different account holder is a third-party payee -> reviewer with four-eyes (my own earlier labels were relabelled).

findings.found: A wholly different account on the form vs the bank letter was treated like a typo; another company's tax registration was treated like an upload slip.
findings.fix: Typo vs different account is measured; a tax ID registered to a differently named company -> reviewer.

findings.found: Honest variants were held: 'M/s' prefix, 'DBA' account titles, 'UG (haftungsbeschraenkt)', swapped upload slots, company PAN with the wrong dropdown.
findings.fix: Recognised as variants or form slips (vendor asked to correct the type); swapped documents are read as what they are.

findings.found: A bank statement was accepted as bank proof; a US domestic account in EUR was accepted.
findings.fix: Statements are recognised and the vendor is asked for a bank letter; a foreign currency on a domestic-only account asks the vendor to confirm.

failures.title: DE clean GmbH, German documents
failures.why_expected: German-language documents are expected for a German vendor and every value matches the form.

failures.title: GB clean Ltd
failures.why_expected: Complete and consistent submission.

failures.title: US clean LLC
failures.why_expected: Complete, consistent W-9 and bank letter.

failures.title: Pvt Ltd vs PRIVATE LIMITED, old GST cert
failures.why_expected: Abbreviation/case differences are harmless and a GST registration certificate does not expire; only the bank proof needs to be recent, and it is.

failures.title: IN sole proprietor paid in own name
failures.why_expected: For a sole proprietorship the proprietor is the legal entity, so a personal-name account and a free email address are normal; all identifiers agree.

failures.title: DE umlaut transliteration
failures.why_expected: ue/ü and ss/ß are the same name in German; everything else matches.

failures.title: GB pays via IBAN only
failures.why_expected: Policy explicitly allows an IBAN in place of sort code + account number, and the IBAN matches the letter.

failures.title: US account titled with DBA
failures.why_expected: The account is held by the same legal entity with its declared DBA; that is a normal title.

failures.title: IN partnership firm with M/s prefix
failures.why_expected: 'M/s' is a customary Indian honorific for firms and '&' vs 'and' is cosmetic; identifiers match.

failures.title: DE bank letter 88 days old
failures.why_expected: 88 days is within the 90-day validity window.

failures.title: GB shares building with existing vendor
failures.why_expected: A shared multi-tenant address alone is not suspicious when name, tax ID, bank and contact are all distinct.

failures.title: US punctuation and case differences
failures.why_expected: Punctuation, capitalisation and Inc/Incorporated are the same entity.

failures.title: DE UG without (haftungsbeschraenkt) on form
failures.why_expected: The parenthetical is part of the legal-form suffix, not a different company.

failures.title: GB clean plc with SWIFT
failures.why_expected: Complete and consistent; a clear photo of the letter is acceptable.

failures.title: US voided check
failures.why_expected: A voided check is acceptable bank proof and matches the form.

failures.title: US name resembles a sanctioned entity
failures.why_expected: A superficial name similarity to a sanctioned metals trader is not a match; different name, industry and identifiers.

failures.title: IN swapped upload slots, common contact name
failures.why_expected: Both required documents were provided and match, just in each other's slots; a common personal name is not a duplicate signal.

failures.title: IN missing bank proof
failures.why_expected: Required bank proof is missing; vendor just needs to upload it.

failures.title: DE bank letter too old
failures.why_expected: Bank proof older than 90 days; vendor must provide a recent one.

failures.title: GB invoice uploaded instead of VAT certificate
failures.why_expected: An invoice is not a VAT registration certificate; the vendor must upload the right document.

failures.title: US blurry W-9 photo
failures.why_expected: Tax form is unreadable; vendor should re-upload a clear copy.

failures.title: IN account number digits transposed
failures.why_expected: Classic keying error with everything else matching; vendor should correct the form rather than anyone paying the typed number.

failures.title: DE IBAN typo fails checksum
failures.why_expected: Invalid IBAN from a typo is a vendor-fixable data error; nothing suspicious.

failures.title: GB VAT number left blank
failures.why_expected: Required form field missing; vendor fills it in.

failures.title: US SSN-shaped number in EIN field
failures.why_expected: Tax ID field is in the wrong format and doesn't match the W-9; vendor should enter the EIN.

failures.title: IN bank statement as bank proof
failures.why_expected: Policy accepts only a bank confirmation letter or cancelled cheque; vendor should upload one of those.

failures.title: DE utility bill as bank proof
failures.why_expected: Wrong document type for bank proof; vendor re-uploads.

failures.title: GB contact email missing
failures.why_expected: Required field missing.

failures.title: US vendor selects EUR currency
failures.why_expected: A domestic US ACH account in EUR is inconsistent; most likely a dropdown slip the vendor should correct.

failures.title: IN GSTIN typo fails checksum
failures.why_expected: Invalid GSTIN from a typo; certificate shows the right one, vendor corrects the field.

failures.title: DE no VAT certificate uploaded
failures.why_expected: Required tax document missing.

failures.title: GB bank letter 91 days old
failures.why_expected: Just outside the 90-day window; vendor needs a fresh letter.

failures.title: IN wrong entity type picked
failures.why_expected: Entity type contradicts the name and GSTIN; a form error the vendor can fix.
